notes: Reconciled from coders A and B. Coder A. Only the four included documents were coded; the 2023 CATLR overview was excluded in the collect file. The university AI policy page is a stub, so its rules are not coded beyond the framework statement. No Khoury College or other computing-unit policy was collected. Several units carry fit notes where a type matched only partly; the provost document's rationale for disclosure (reflection) and common-syllabus rule are UNCOVERED. Coder B. Only the four included documents were coded; neu-catlr-2023 was screened out. The AI Policy page (neu-ai-policy) is a stub; the full Policy on the Use of AI Systems was not in the collected text. Integrity-policy units on sanctions, appeals and reporting are generic to all violations and were coded because AI use is classed there as cheating. Unit stance for sample labels is that of the label itself. Reconciler: unit_stance for disclosure or documentation requirements was left as the coders agreed (require) where they both said so; the codebook reserves require for built-in or required AI use, so the theme review may want to recheck those units.

documents.title: Standards and Recommendations for the Use of Generative AI in Teaching and Learning at Northeastern
documents.stance_why: The Standards say they 'respect instructor autonomy', give no university-wide rule, and offer sample syllabus statements ('AI Use Encouraged', 'Sometimes Allowed', 'Not Permitted') and assignment labels (Prohibited, Permitted, Encouraged, Required). A document that hands the decision to instructors and offers tiers is delegates under the codebook.
documents.summary: Provost and CATLR standards for faculty on generative AI in teaching. They leave the decision to each instructor, ask for clear communication and attribution, advise against detectors and give sample syllabus statements and assignment labels.
